prompt:
Draw a new 4-frame native-pixel baseball sprite production strip, four full-body consecutive INBETWEEN poses on perfectly flat #FF00FF magenta. This strip covers ONLY the short hand-lift arc from completed swing shoulder height to above helmet. It does not cover the whole recovery and MUST NOT skip ahead to READY or lower hands to waist.
Image1 is accepted native adult batter identity/style/camera. Image2 is the motion START: both gloves at image-left shoulder, wooden bat across behind shoulders. Image3 is the TARGET endpoint: both gloves above helmet centre, bat foreshortened almost directly away from camera. Image4 is only a 4slot layout guide.
Draw four evenly spaced NEW inbetweens BETWEEN image2 and image3. No duplicates of start/end. Fixed elevated umpire rear camera, face hidden, same helmet, ivory uniform/navy sleeves and socks. Body, shoes and pelvis scale unchanged. Rear support right foot remains large low-left, left lead foot higher-right, knees slightly bent, weight shifts gradually to balance.
HAND PATH: from the start at upper-left chest, move the two joined gloves up and to the right along the LEFT EDGE of helmet, then around above the left crown, ending just left of the target. Frame0: hands move only one small step up, beside left cheek/temple, bat still partly across behind shoulders but 3D-shortening. Frame1: hands one small step above the left temple, barrel partly hidden behind upper helmet, short angled wooden segment visible. Frame2: hands above upper-left crown, elbows naturally lifted, barrel points strongly away and appears short/end-on. Frame3: hands above crown but still slightly left of image3 target, bat end-on, leaving one small step to image3. Each glove-centre shift about10–15storage pixels (these are between endpoint references separated about50px). Do NOT make frame0 a copy of start finish. Do NOT jump to target overhead in frame1. Do NOT return hands to image-right shoulder in any of these four frames. The future strip already owns that arc.
The bat turns in depth: a single straight bat, shortened by perspective and partially occluded behind the helmet. Never draw a long full stick sweeping through helmet, torso or hands. Two hands must remain joined on the handle, connected by plausible forearms to shoulders. Torso gradually untwists slightly, not flipping to a frontal face. Distinct four poses with exact consistent anatomy, clean128logical pixel clusters enlarged2x storage, three-value material planes, selective cool navy outline, same shadows as references, no fine painted texture. Full-body and entire visible bat inside each invisible slot, no clipping/slot crossing. No text, grid, numbers, floor, cast shadows, ball, blur, motion arcs or FX. Output just the image.
